description: Verifies polarized radiative transfer: Stokes vector invariants and frame rotation, Bessel functions and the Maxwell-Juttner distribution, the polarization degree of power-law synchrotron emission and absorption, thermal bremsstrahlung and its Gaunt factor, the analytic and Runge-Kutta transfer steps, and inverse Compton scattering against the Thomson limit.

checks.label: a fully linearly polarized vector is physically valid
the intensity is the first component
the linearly polarized intensity equals sqrt(Q^2 + U^2)
the fractional linear polarization equals 1
the electric vector position angle equals half of atan2(U, Q)
the intensity is invariant under a frame rotation
a quarter-turn rotation of the position angle exchanges Q and U
a quarter-turn rotation of the position angle changes the sign of the old Q
K0(1) lies between 0.4 and 0.5
K1(1) lies between 0.5 and 0.7
K2(1) lies between 1.5 and 1.8
the recurrence K2(x) = 2 K1(x) / x + K0(x) holds at x = 1
the mean Lorentz factor at theta = 1 lies between 3 and 4
every sampled Lorentz factor is at least 1
the sample mean agrees with the analytic mean within 0.1
the linear polarization of a power law with p = 3 equals (p + 1) / (p + 7/3)
the linear polarization for p = 3 equals 0.75
the linear polarization for p = 2 equals 9/13
the absorption coefficients are positive
the absorption polarization equals the emission polarization for a power law
the bremsstrahlung emissivity is positive
the thermal Gaunt factor lies between 0.5 and 20
the analytic Delano step yields a physically valid Stokes vector
the analytic step builds up positive intensity
the analytic step builds up linear polarization
the Runge-Kutta step builds up positive intensity
the Klein-Nishina cross section tends to the Thomson value at low energy within a relative 1e-3
the Compton y parameter is positive
scattering preserves the number of photon packets
scattering off hot electrons raises the mean photon energy
